title: A Tumultuous Assembly. Numerical Sensibility
lede: A words-in-freedom plate in which F. T. Marinetti builds a shouting figure from giant letters and surrounds it with tilted columns of printed numbers, prices, and tables.
summary: A figure built from huge letters, hooks, and numbers among tilted columns of tabular type. F. T. Marinetti, 1919.

source.label: The Metropolitan Museum of Art: Une Assemblée tumultueuse. Sensibilité numérique (1995.511.2)

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the Met’s image as uploaded to [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A_Tumultuous_Assembly._Numerical_Sensibility_(Une_Assembl%C3%A9e_tumultueuse._Sensibilit%C3%A9_num%C3%A9rique)_published_in_Les_mots_en_libert%C3%A9_futuristes_MET_DP371750.jpg) (original 3917 × 3127 px; a 1280 × 1022 px rendering was inspected and stored). The physical copy is the Met’s sheet, accession number 1995.511.2, as stated in the Commons record.

styles.note: Words in freedom with the Futurist love of numbers: tables, prices, and giant digits at many angles, assembled into a figure.

context: Letterpress, 26.7 × 33.0 cm, published in 1919 in *Les mots en liberté futuristes*. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Drawings and Prints, 1995.511.2, gift of W. Michael Sheehe, 1995. [Commons record from the Met](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:A_Tumultuous_Assembly._Numerical_Sensibility_(Une_Assembl%C3%A9e_tumultueuse._Sensibilit%C3%A9_num%C3%A9rique)_published_in_Les_mots_en_libert%C3%A9_futuristes_MET_DP371750.jpg).
The same book contains [Le Soir, couchée dans son lit](ref:marinetti-le-soir-couchee-dans-son-lit-1919).
observed: At the center, a standing figure is built from a giant black “P”, a long black hook like an arm or a mouth, the word “ANCHUZ” in heavy capitals, and a large “5” as the legs.
Inside the hook, small columns of text run along its length.
Columns of tiny numbers and words, like tables or price lists, are pasted at many angles across the whole sheet.
Large isolated letters and numbers stand around the edges: “MA”, “T”, “A5”, “M”, “Z”, “1”, “10”, “1918 918!”.
At right, letters such as “O”, “ZZ”, and “E” are set inside black discs, and a clock face appears among them.
Prices and quantities such as “50 mila”, “50.000”, “5000”, and “del 100 per 100” are set in medium sizes at different tilts.
Printed in black only on buff paper with a center fold.
interpretation: The page treats a crowd as data: the “assembly” is made of numbers, statistics, and prices, and the shouting figure at the center is a typographic puppet. It anticipates the mechanical figures of the 1920s that the style record describes.
The tilted tables show how even dense, small text can become texture and motion when it is set at angles.
borrow: Build a figure or mascot from giant letters and numbers.
Use tables of small numbers as a tilted background texture behind large type.
Put single letters inside solid circles as accents.

images.alt: Black letterpress on buff paper: a figure built from a giant letter P, a long black hook, the word ANCHUZ, and a large 5 stands among tilted columns of tiny numbers and tables. Large letters and numbers, digits in black discs, and a clock face surround it.

rights.statement: The Metropolitan Museum of Art released the image under CC0 through its Open Access programme. Marinetti was Italian and died in 1944, more than 70 years ago, so the work is public domain in Italy. It was published in 1919, before 1931, so it is public domain in the United States.
